attendance: 19,084 total attendance in 2024, of which 2,424 exhibitors and 1,014 guests/press
attendance_rung_name: exhibitor prospectus with full attendee demographics
attendance_method: WebFetch failed on the PDF (12.5 MB, over the size cap), so I downloaded it with curl and extracted the text. Page with the booth-payment section carries a sidebar headed '2024 Attendance Figures: 19,084' with a full breakdown: Dentists 5,001; Dental Students 4,484; Dental Hygienists 2,540; Exhibitors 2,424; Dental Assistants 1,957; Office Personnel 1,493; Guests/Press 1,014; Medical Professionals 136; Technicians 30. Note this is a registered-body count for a trade show, not delegates at a scientific congress. Discounting exhibitor staff (2,424) and guests/press (1,014) gives roughly 15,600 dental professionals and students. A 28,000 figure circulating in search snippets (attributed to the convention centre) did not appear on any page I loaded; the 2026 Dentistry Today preview I fetched via curl states no number at all.
ratio_rationale: Judged 0.5% — the new floor — on the single ground that almost no contributed science happens at this meeting, not on who attends. I have removed my earlier reasoning about the student and assistant share of the room: students present abstracts everywhere else in this workbook and it was wrong to treat them as evidence of a low rate. The real evidence is the programme: I loaded yankeedental.com/about/ and its FAQ and found no call for abstracts, no author guidelines, no poster or paper session and no scientific-programme language of any kind; the Dentistry Today preview describes only CE courses, hands-on learning, panel discussions, an exhibit floor and a concert. The only plausible submitted content is a student table-clinic competition, which is tens of entries, not hundreds — which is why the floor rather than zero. The 19,084 headline is also trade-show padded (2,424 exhibitor staff, 1,014 guests/press), exactly the case the lowered floor exists for. Previously recorded as 2%, which on this headcount would have implied around 380 abstracts — not a number I believe.
programme_evidence: Dentistry Today 2026 preview (loaded via curl): 'A wide range of continuing education courses, including hands-on learning experiences... Lectures and panel discussions led by innovative industry experts' plus 'Hundreds of exhibitors' and an evening concert. No scientific session type named.
character_evidence: https://www.yankeedental.com/about/ and https://www.yankeedental.com/about/frequently-asked-questions/ — both loaded; continuing-education course framing throughout, no call for abstracts or author guidelines anywhere on the site sections I opened.

conference: DGIM Kongress (German Society of Internal Medicine)
attendance: more than 8,500 participants on site and online at the 132nd congress (2026); roughly 80% in person
attendance_rung_name: post-congress press coverage of the society's closing release
attendance_method: Loaded the post-congress report, which states 'Mit mehr als 8.500 Teilnehmenden vor Ort und online ist der 132. Kongress der Deutschen Gesellschaft für Innere Medizin (DGIM) zu Ende gegangen' and notes roughly 80% attended in person, 20% remotely — so the on-site figure is about 6,800 and the 8,500 headline is virtual-inclusive. The same page gives the programme scale: '451 Sitzungen mit rund 1.300 Referierenden'. Search snippets also offered ~9,000 for the 131st (2025) and ~8,300 for the 125th; I did not load those pages so they are not recorded as figures.
ratio_rationale: Judged 7% of the full 8,500, including the roughly 1,700 online participants — revised under the updated rule: I had previously converted only the ~6,800 on-site share, which was wrong, since a remote attendee can present a poster as readily as anyone in Wiesbaden. The judgement itself is unchanged and rests on programme shape: the DGIM Internistenkongress is the German-speaking world's flagship continuing-education meeting for internal medicine, with 451 sessions carried by around 1,300 invited Referierende, so the great majority of what happens there is commissioned teaching and the free-paper/poster stream is a modest bolt-on. That sits just above EuroPCR (6%), our teaching-course anchor, and below AAD (9%) and PAS (9%), both broad specialty congresses with visibly larger contributed programmes than DGIM's.
programme_evidence: '451 Sitzungen mit rund 1.300 Referierenden' — an invited-speaker-dominated Fortbildung programme; the closing release highlights themed teaching tracks, not submitted science.
character_evidence: Congress is CME/Fortbildung-framed throughout the closing report, but DGIM does run a free-paper and poster call alongside it; no submission page loaded this round.

attendance: 6,881 total registrations at ESHG 2025 (Milan), from over 94 countries
attendance_method: I first loaded the society's own past-meetings page (https://www.eshg.org/conferences/past-eshg-meetings) — it lists venues and abstract supplements but no attendance numbers. The figure comes from a loaded recap page stating 'Total registrations reached 6,881' and 'nearly 7,000 total registrations from over 94 countries'. This is a registration count for a hybrid conference and the source does not split in-person from virtual, so the on-site delegate number is lower; basis UNSPECIFIED and this is a third-party recap, not the society, hence MEDIUM. A pre-conference expectation of 3,000 delegates also circulated in snippets; not confirmed on a loaded page.
ratio_rationale: Judged 45%, revised up from 40% under the updated rule: I had previously held the figure down partly because the 6,881 is a registration count with a virtual tail, which is no longer a reason to discount — an abstract presented online still counts. On shape alone ESHG belongs at the top of the research-society band: it is a genetics congress whose programme is dominated by submitted work, with concurrent and e-poster sessions built almost entirely from the abstract book, and groups sending whole teams precisely because each member has a poster. That is ESCMID's shape (40%) pushed a little higher, and it approaches ECR (48%) and ATS (50%); I stopped short of those because a commercial diagnostics-lab contingent attends ESHG in numbers and much of it is there to sell rather than to submit.
programme_evidence: ESHG publishes a full abstract supplement for every meeting (linked from the society's past-meetings page for every year 2001-2025), and the conference programme is organised around concurrent sessions drawn from submitted abstracts.
character_evidence: https://www.eshg.org/conferences/past-eshg-meetings — abstract publications listed for every meeting 2001-2025, i.e. a standing open call.

BIO is a business-development and partnering convention: its own by-the-numbers page sells the audience on C-suite share and purchasing authority, and the programme is invited company sessions plus 60,000+ one-to-one partnering meetings. There is no call for abstracts to convert, and the headline is a registrant count heavily padded with exhibiting-company staff and trade-show visitors — precisely the case the lowered floor is for. Even EuroPCR at 6%, a teaching course, sits inside a scientific society and overstates this row by an order of magnitude.
programme_evidence: convention.bio.org by-the-numbers page markets attendee seniority and purchasing authority; the convention is structured around 180+ curated sessions, 1,100 invited speakers and 60,000+ partnering meetings.
character_evidence: https://convention.bio.org/about-bio/bio-2025-numbers — no abstracts or poster sessions mentioned; programme is invited sessions plus the partnering system.

programme_evidence: Meeting is framed around plenaries, leadership development and community sessions for academic medicine, with an education-research poster strand rather than an abstract-driven core.
character_evidence: AAMC runs an annual call for proposals/abstracts for Learn Serve Lead sessions and posters alongside a largely invited plenary programme; submission page not loaded this round.

attendance: 546 total attendance in 2024 (American College of Clinical Pharmacology, Bethesda MD) — SEE AMBIGUITY NOTE
attendance_rung_name: organiser's post-meeting registration and demographics report
attendance_method: IDENTITY WARNING FOR THE ORCHESTRATOR: 'ACCP Annual Meeting' is ambiguous. Two different US societies run a meeting under that exact name — the American College of Clinical PharmacoLOGY (accp1.org) and the American College of Clinical PharmacY (accp.com). The umbrella on this row ('Pharmacology & pharmacy') does not disambiguate. The figure I confirmed is for the PharmacoLOGY meeting: WebFetch got a 403, so I downloaded the 2024 Annual Meeting Registration and Demographics Report with curl and read it with pdftotext. Its 'Total Attendance' table reads: 2024 Bethesda MD 546; 2023 Bellevue WA 482; 2022 Bethesda MD 433; 2021 Virtual 367; 2020 Virtual 433; 2019 Chicago IL 409; 2018 Bethesda MD 458 — with a geographic split of 485 United States / 61 international. For the PharmacY meeting (accp.com) I could not confirm any attendance figure: its exhibitor material is behind a prospectus request and no loaded page carried a number. That meeting is substantially larger and if this row is meant to be the PharmacY one, this 546 badly understates it and the row needs a separate look.
ratio_rationale: Judged 40% for the PharmacoLOGY meeting the figure belongs to, revised up from 35%: I had held it down on the grounds that the large industry and CRO contingent attends to recruit and sell, which was the wrong kind of reasoning — industry and CRO scientists at a clinical pharmacology meeting are authors on posters as a matter of course. On shape this is a small research-society meeting of 546 people, its demographics report showing 33% academia alongside substantial CRO, industry and government shares, and the society's own exhibitor page describes the programme as built on 'Poster Sessions, Evening Receptions, Industry Theater presentations'. Small scientific societies convert high because presenting is the reason to travel — that is the ESCMID (40%) pattern, a touch above ASN (35%).
programme_evidence: accp1.org exhibitor page (loaded via curl): the meeting is structured around 'Poster Sessions, Evening Receptions, Industry Theater presentations, breakfasts, coffee breaks' alongside educational symposia and plenary sessions.
character_evidence: Meeting abstracts are published annually in Clinical Pharmacology in Drug Development (accp1.onlinelibrary.wiley.com hosts an 'ACCP meeting abstracts' collection); poster sessions are a named programme element on the exhibitor page.

The World Health Summit is a global health policy summit whose programme is entirely invited — 300+ speakers on curated panels for an audience of ministers, agency heads, funders, NGO staff and industry — and I found no call for abstracts on any page I loaded. Honest uncertainty: if WHS runs a poster or young-researcher stream I did not surface, the true figure could be several times this; 1% is my most likely reading on the evidence I have, and it sits below EuroPCR (6%), our lowest counted anchor, because EuroPCR at least converts part of its room into submitted science.

character_evidence: https://www.worldhealthsummit.org/impact — programme described entirely in terms of invited speakers and stakeholder convening; no call for abstracts surfaced on any page I loaded.

attendance: about 750 physicians and scientists, approximately 10% international
attendance_method: Loaded AAST's own event page for the 85th Annual Meeting (Dallas, September 2026): 'The meeting attracts about 750 physicians and scientists whose primary interest lies in the investigation and the treatment of various forms of trauma and the application of surgical critical care' and 'Approximately 10% of the attendees come from Europe, South America, Asia and Africa'. The society reports approximately 2,100 members from 130 countries. The 750 is explicitly physicians and scientists, so it is a clean DELEGATES basis with no exhibitor padding — but it is a recurring characterisation, not a dated count, so no year can be pinned. A search snippet asserting '1,500 attendees' came from a third-party booth-cost site and did not appear on any page I loaded; not recorded.
ratio_rationale: Judged 50%, level with ATS (50%) and just above ECR (48%) — and the reasoning is the shape of the meeting rather than its subject. AAST is a small, invitation-tight academic surgical society whose Annual Meeting programme is almost entirely competitively selected submitted papers, published as the trauma literature's main annual dump in the Journal of Trauma and Acute Care Surgery; the 750 in the room are described by the society itself as 'physicians and scientists whose primary interest lies in the investigation' of trauma, i.e. a room of investigators, not a CME audience. That is the same converting logic as our highest non-trivial anchors, and only the Clinical Congress of Acute Care Surgery running alongside it — which does draw non-presenting clinical attendees — keeps me from going into the SOT 46%-and-above small-society band in full.
programme_evidence: Society event page leads with 'Online Abstract Submission' and describes the audience as investigators; the annual meeting's papers are published as a block in the Journal of Trauma and Acute Care Surgery.
character_evidence: https://www.aast.org/ems-event-calendar/85th-annual-meeting-of-aast-clinical-congress-of-acute-care-surgery.html — 'Online Abstract Submission' link on the meeting page.
